Right, since nobody has any questions I want to clarify my idea for a forum in the city of the local district. Really it's a simple idea. There is a subreddit for the city where anybody can go to discuss and debate topics relative to the city. There would be no mechanism for legally binding resolutions initially but with time I could see allowing it. It will be a pure democracy where every participant has a vote in any suggestion made.  There will be one thread per week with discussion. Topics can be submitted before the start of the thread. Each topic will part of a single comment in the thread for simplicity. So if for example, person x submits topic y prior to the thread, then person x comments with their stance on topic y and all discussion of topic y is limited to replies of that comment.  This is really just to keep discussion organized. Any topic not submitted and put on the agenda may be commented in the thread and added to the agenda, but everybody must still discuss the idea as a response to that first comment.  There will be a forum head, whose job it is to post the thread and run the session. Rules and bylaws for elections will be determined by general consensus in the first session. I will be the first forum head (if elected) and then a new forum head will be elected in no more than 3 weeks from my taking office. This way the forum will be independent before my term is over.  There will be bylaws for proposing and voting on a referendum. These bylaws will all be determined by the forum after it is formed.  The entire point of the forum is not to run the city but to instead discuss the city, what the goals for the city should be, and make recommendations on how to achieve those goals. The reason I don't want a Memechester style city council is twofold. First, I want to experiment with other forms of democracy, cities can be test grounds for ideas the same way states are test grounds in the US. Second, and I will be very blunt here, I don't like letting a council decide production order and being required to follow it. It feels too much like I am ignoring my judgment in favor of the judgment of a crowd.   The forum, I believe, offers a good compromise between the unilateral decision making present in most cities and what best seems to be the organized chaos of a city council. The forum allows for large input in times where it is needed and next to no input when the city is running smoothly. It allows for people to discuss the direction of the city and what they believe the goals should be, without getting too bogged down in the business of running the city. You decide what you want to see from the city and let me achieve it for you.
